la:verb:volito.html:
vŏlĭto, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. freq. n. [2. volo], to fly to and fro, to fly or flit about, to flutter (class.).
Lit.: aves volitare,: (volucris) propter humum volitat,: volitant alii (scarabaei) magno cum murmure,. —
Transf., to fly, hasten, or hover about; to flutter, float about: volitans totā acie,: mediis in millibus ductores,: volitabit et vagabitur in foro,; cf.: totā Asiā vagatur, volitat ut rex,: volitare in foro,: volitat ante oculos istorum Jubae regis filius,: pacatum volitant per mare navitae,: tribuni praefectique cum terrore et armatorum catervis volitabant,; cf. . —Of things concr. and abstr.: quae (rerum simulacra) quasi membranae summo de corpore rerum Dereptae volitant ultro citroque per auras,; cf. : solidissima materiaï Corpora perpetuo volitare,hover, float about,; so of atoms,; ; : stellae,: atra favilla in nimbo,: umbrae inter vivos,: circum litora,: et tenues animae volitare silentum,: voces per auras,.—
Trop., to fly, fly or flutter about, fly to and fro, etc.: nemo me lacrimis decoret nec funera fletu Faxit. Cur? Volito vivu' per ora virūm, Enn. ap. ; cf. (Epigr. v. 4, p. 162 Vahl.): speremus nostrum nomen volitare et vagari latissime,: si nostri animi ... gestiant ac volitare cupiant vacui curā ac labore,to wander about,: valebis apud hominem volitantem gloriae cupiditate, vir moderatus et constans,soaring, aspiring,; cf.: cupis volitare per auras,: nec volitabo in hoc insolentius, fly into a passion, Cic. Fl. 16, 38: (Clodius) volitat, furit,.
